done_looks_like: Running `config-diff a.json b.json` on the example pair under examples/ prints a numbered, JSON-path-keyed diff to stdout, accepts numeric indices on stdin, writes a.patched.json, and exits 0; the written file is byte-identical to examples/expected-patched.json.
Malformed or unreadable inputs cause the CLI to print a single error line naming the offending file and exit non-zero, without touching any output path.
Inputs are read-only: after any successful or failed run, the SHA-256 of both input files matches what it was before invocation.

Diff output is grep-able (one diff entry per line prefixed by its numeric index and JSONPath) and the exit code is 0 on clean apply, non-zero on parse/IO failure, so the tool composes into shell pipelines.

MODULE config_diff/parser.py (applicability: cross-system-integration / ACL for stdlib `json` + filesystem) hides_decision: 'parser.py owns how raw JSON bytes from a filesystem path become an in-memory tree plus a single normalized ParseError, isolating callers from json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, and OSError shape drift.' Entry-point budget: 1 (`load(path: Path) -> ParsedConfig`). Broad interface: invariant = path must exist before call (caller's responsibility, surfaced as ParseError if not); ordering = none (stateless); error modes = exactly one ParseError(path, reason) class covering not-found / permission-denied / invalid-encoding / invalid-json. No Strategy seam (one concrete impl; two-adapter rule per C5 not met for any alternate loader this sprint).

MODULE config_diff/differ.py (applicability: business-logic) hides_decision: 'differ.py owns the JSON-path enumeration + value-comparison algorithm that turns two ParsedConfig trees into an ordered list of DiffEntry records, including the canonical sort order and added/removed/changed classification.' Entry-point budget: 1 (`diff(left: ParsedConfig, right: ParsedConfig) -> list[DiffEntry]`). Broad interface: invariant = output ordering is deterministic and total (depth-first over sorted keys, list indices ascending); ordering = none on caller side (pure function); error modes = no exceptions — non-JSON inputs are already filtered by parser.py. No Strategy seam.

MODULE config_diff/applier.py (applicability: business-logic) hides_decision: 'applier.py owns how a subset of DiffEntry records (a patch plan) is applied onto the target tree to produce a new tree, including conflict resolution rules and the immutability guarantee that the input tree is not mutated.' Entry-point budget: 1 (`apply(target: ParsedConfig, plan: list[DiffEntry]) -> ParsedConfig`). Broad interface: invariant = input `target` is never mutated (returns new tree); ordering = plan entries are applied in their list order; error modes = exactly one ApplyError(entry, reason) class for path-no-longer-exists / type-conflict; deletion-test commitment: at least 2 distinct callers (CLI + applier unit tests) would re-grow the path-walk + immutable-update logic if applier were removed.

MODULE config_diff/cli.py (applicability: framework-shaped — typer command; opt-out of deep-module C1-C8 per foundation.md §3 row 'Framework-mandated shape') is a thin wiring layer: it composes parser.load + differ.diff + interactive selection prompt + applier.apply + atomic write to output path. No business logic lives here; this is the only place where stdin/stdout I/O happens.
Bounded context: the entire codebase is one BC (`config-diff`); no external system other than stdlib + filesystem is crossed, so the only ACL is parser.py at the json/filesystem boundary.
Inner-gate-clean commit: ruff format + ruff check + mypy --strict + pytest unit suite + verification-step id literal-coverage all GREEN at the commit that closes the sprint.

verification_plan.expected_outcome: All parser unit tests pass: happy path returns ParsedConfig; missing file / permission denied / invalid UTF-8 / invalid JSON each raise ParseError with the offending path embedded. Tests do not import json.JSONDecodeError (interface hides it).

All differ unit tests pass: empty-vs-empty -> []; added-only / removed-only / changed-only / mixed cases produce DiffEntry lists in the documented deterministic order; nested dicts and lists are diffed by JSONPath; renaming an internal helper inside differ.py does not break any test (C7 interface-as-test-surface check).

All applier unit tests pass: empty plan returns input unchanged (deep-equal but not identity if applier rebuilds); applying full diff produces right-tree byte-equivalent JSON; partial plan applies only selected entries; input `target` object is not mutated (assert post-call deep-equal to pre-call snapshot); path-no-longer-exists / type-conflict raise ApplyError.
